one_liner: Bun-first TypeScript web framework; ties actix-web on a hello-world GET because Bun serves that route natively.
what_it_does: Elysia is a TypeScript HTTP framework built for the Bun runtime: a chained route builder (`new Elysia().get('/', handler).listen(3000)`) with lifecycle hooks, plugins, TypeBox (`t`) or Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot) validation, OpenAPI generation and a typed client (Eden). It is not a drop-in for actix-web; adopting it means rewriting a Rust service in TypeScript and running it on Bun. Node.js (Node adapter `@elysia/node`, formerly `@elysiajs/node`) and Cloudflare Workers (experimental adapter) are supported, but the default Bun adapter's `.listen()` throws unless Bun is present.
how_it_is_fast: On Bun, `listen()` hands every route to `Bun.serve({ routes })`, Bun's native router (built on uWebSockets' tree router). A handler given as a constant value, such as `.get('/', '')`, is turned into a pre-built `Response` (`nativeStaticResponse`, on by default) that Bun dispatches with zero allocation and without running any JavaScript per request. For function handlers, Elysia's JIT 'AOT' step (sucrose) reads each handler's source with `Function.prototype.toString()` to infer which of query/headers/body/cookie it uses, then emits a specialised handler compiled with `new Function()` that skips unused parsing. `SO_REUSEPORT` is on by default, so one Bun process per core can share a port.
when_to_use: You already run Bun and want the lowest-overhead typed TypeScript framework: in the 2026-09-24 run elysia-bun did 173,877 req/s at c=512 vs hono-deno 130,540, fastify 68,128 and express 42,586.
Fixed-content endpoints (health checks, version strings, redirects) that Elysia can hand to Bun as static responses.
TypeScript teams that want one schema to drive runtime validation, OpenAPI docs and a typed frontend client without a codegen step.
Linux hosts where you can run one Bun process per core behind SO_REUSEPORT (cluster mode).
when_not_to_use: As a reason to move off actix-web: on this suite it ties (0.96x-1.06x across c=64-512, 0.97x-0.995x in two earlier snapshots), and actix had lower p99 at c=64 (0.4 ms vs 0.7 ms).
On Node.js: the same app through `@elysiajs/node` did 48,128 req/s at c=512, about 0.29x actix and 0.28x elysia-bun.
Handler-heavy services (DB calls, JSON bodies, validation): the benchmark route is a pre-built static response, so it gives no evidence about Elysia's per-request code path.
Very large typed APIs where editor speed matters: open issue #1031 reports 10-20 s IntelliSense delays; one reporter has 202 plugins and 1,168 endpoints.

Large multipart uploads through the built-in parser: open issue #1744 reports a memory leak on 1.4.22, and the form-data normalizer was quadratic in the number of fields until 1.4.29 (CVE-2026-56669).

integration.form: module (npm package `elysia`, ESM and CJS builds)
integration.dependencies: cookie, exact-mirror, fast-decode-uri-component, memoirist; peers @sinclair/typebox >=0.34 <1, file-type >=20, openapi-types >=12, exact-mirror; optional peers @types/bun >=1.2, typescript >=5.0; Node needs the @elysia/node adapter
integration.min_toolchain: Bun (peer @types/bun >=1.2; the benchmark used Bun 1.4); TypeScript >=5.0 for type-checking; package.json has no engines field
integration.platforms: Wherever Bun runs (Elysia does not list platforms); Node.js via adapter; Cloudflare Workers adapter is experimental; SO_REUSEPORT port sharing works only on Linux per the deploy docs
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded per process ('Elysia is single-threaded by default'); scale out with cluster mode, one process per core

gotchas: Constant-value routes (`.get('/', '')`) become native Bun static Responses built once at `listen()`; that is exactly the-benchmarker's GET / route, so its numbers measure Bun's static dispatch. Any `onRequest` or trace hook, or a higher-order function, disables these native static routes app-wide.

AOT builds handlers as source strings run through `new Function()`. Unescaped schema property names and defaults allowed remote code execution (GHSA-gmm9-qwx3-2m3h, critical, <=1.4.29, listed as fixed in the 1.4.30 changelog); cookie config injection was CVE-2025-66457. Never build schemas from untrusted input and stay on >=1.4.30.
AOT can regress badly: issue #1604 measured 3,853 req/s with defaults vs 175,951 with `aot: false` on 1.4.18 because `fetch` was recompiled per request (fixed in 1.4.19).

Docs and code disagree: the configuration page says `aot` defaults to false, but the source enables it unless `ELYSIA_AOT=false`. Official packages moved from the `@elysiajs/*` npm scope to `@elysia/*` in 2026, and 2.0 is in beta (2.0.0-beta.19 on the npm `next` tag), so expect renames and breaking changes.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Elysia over hyper, Jooby or ActiveJ only when the service must be TypeScript on Bun; all four sit within about -4% to +9% of actix on this route. If raw JavaScript throughput is the only goal, fulmine.js posted more (203,996 req/s at c=512) in the same run.
verified_claims_summary: In the-benchmarker/web-frameworks run of 2026-09-24 (commit f673364; empty GET /, zrk closed-loop keep-alive, server limited to about 4 of 16 x86-64 cores on Linux 7.2, CPU model not recorded), Elysia 1.4 on Bun 1.4 (one process per CPU) did 172,228 / 174,958 / 173,877 req/s at c=64/256/512 vs actix-web 4.8 (Rust 1.98, LTO, opt-level 3) at 179,203 / 168,270 / 163,415, i.e. 0.96x-1.06x, and was 0.97x-0.995x in the two earlier snapshots: a tie. The Elysia route is a constant, so Bun served a pre-built Response without running Elysia code; the suite's raw-Bun entry, which uses a JavaScript callback per request, did 145,897 req/s at c=512.
status_note: Actively maintained (1.4.30 released 2026-08-26, about 1.24M npm downloads a week, MIT), but 2.0 is in beta and there are six public security advisories since December 2025 (two critical) plus four more fixed in 1.4.30, so pin versions and track releases.
